description: This Global Platform for Sustainable Cities publication presents six case studies of climate-smart infrastructure projects that promote green and resilient urban development, three international and three from Türkiye. They were selected from a longer list to support World Bank lending to Turkish cities. The publication groups lessons into policy and finance, planning and design, and processes and partnerships; key success factors include aligning project design criteria with international and national financing requirements, using public sector influence for large projects, integrating individual projects under a single strategy as in Vienna's Smart Climate City Strategy and İzmir's waterfront design strategy, and phasing complex projects to spread financial risk and build capacity. Coverage is Türkiye plus international comparators. Format and access: a report linked from the GPSC knowledge product page. Licence: not read; free. Caveats: only the page summary was read because the site challenges scripts, so the full list of cases and the publication date are not recorded. It supports climate adaptation and capacity planning of urban infrastructure programmes in Turkish municipalities. A related catalogue record is the SUEN benchmarking of Türkiye's metropolitan water utilities.
